1301.author: HongyeZhou
1301.body:
## Problem

Version numbers of an Artifact came from one number instead of from the versions actually stored: `createArtifactVersion` used `artifact.currentVersion + 1` and an import wrote a package's own numbering with no uniqueness check (`services/api/src/store.ts`). A catalogue where the pointer lagged behind the versions on disk (written by an older build, restored, merged by hand) handed out a number that already existed, and an import could re-create a collision outright. Two versions of one Artifact then both read as "v3", so the version list, `latestReportVersion`, research-snapshot copies, by-number lookups and every reference that pins `(artifactId, version)` became ambiguous.

## Change

- `createArtifactVersion` allocates `max(highest stored number, artifact.currentVersion) + 1`, skipping numbers already stored for that Artifact, so a lagging pointer cannot hand out an existing number. A pointer that is not a whole number is treated as `0` instead of turning the allocation into `NaN`.
- `load()` normalises a catalogue that already holds duplicates: within one Artifact the first number in `(createdAt, id)` order is kept, every later collision moves above that Artifact's highest number, and `currentVersion` is lifted to the highest number that actually exists. Lifting the pointer also removes the false `ARTIFACT_VERSION_CONFLICT` that a lagging pointer produced when the newest version was published as an edit.
- The normalisation skips Artifacts whose numbers are all usable and unique, so a well-formed catalogue is not touched, and it tolerates hand-edited data: only safe positive integers count as numbers, a missing or non-string `createdAt`/`id` no longer throws while ordering, and a `currentVersion` that is not a whole number is reset before the per-Artifact lift. Without that, one malformed row made `load()` reject (the API could not start), three rows without usable numbers made it loop forever, and a deleted pointer survived every reload.
- An import keeps the package's numbers exactly, because `research-snapshot-integrity` compares each `version` and `currentVersion` and because provenance (`evidenceItems[].origin.artifactVersion`, numeric memory-graph properties) resolves by number. The package is validated before any session, Artifact or version is created: a number that is not a positive integer is refused with `ARTIFACT_VERSION_INVALID` (the restore would skip it and leave the provisional number behind, which collides just as badly) and a number used twice for one Artifact with `ARTIFACT_VERSION_DUPLICATE`, so a refused import leaves no partial catalog behind.

I renumbered on load instead of refusing to load: the issue leaves that sub-question to the maintainer, and a refusal would strand every session whose catalogue already has such a version. No version ID changes, so dependencies and references are untouched.

## Tests

`services/api/src/store.test.ts`:

- `Artifact versions are numbered above the stored versions, not from a stale currentVersion pointer` writes `currentVersion: 0` into the persisted catalogue after two versions exist, expects the pointer to be lifted to `2` on load, and expects an edit published against the newest version to succeed as `3` (that path used to fail as a stale base).
- `a catalog holding duplicate Artifact version numbers is renumbered on load` writes two versions under number `1`, expects `[1, 2]` after `load()`, the same numbers and IDs on a second load, and the next allocation to be `3`.
- `an import keeps the package's own version numbers` restores a normally numbered package onto a fresh Artifact and asserts `[1, 2]` with `currentVersion === 2` (the numbers `createArtifactVersion` provisionally allocated must not shift), then `5` while free (`[1, 5]`).
- `a package with a repeated or unusable Artifact version number is rejected before anything is created` (`research-package-http.test.ts`) rebuilds the evidence package twice — two versions under number `1`, then `[0, 1]` — posts each to a fresh project, expects `400` with `ARTIFACT_VERSION_DUPLICATE` and `ARTIFACT_VERSION_INVALID`, and asserts the project still has no Artifacts.
- `a catalog with malformed version numbers and timestamps still loads` writes a non-numeric number, a missing `createdAt` and a duplicate, expects three distinct usable numbers, then deletes `currentVersion`, reloads, and expects the pointer to be lifted and the next allocation to be a real integer.

The first, second and last fail on the base revision; the package case fails when the up-front validation is stashed, and the import-numbering case failed on the renumbering variant reviewed at `cc407a35`.

## Verification

- `pnpm ci:l1` — PASS, planned 4 / passed 4 / failed 0
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` at the repository root, and `pnpm typecheck` in `services/api` — clean
- `node --import tsx --test src/store.test.ts` in `services/api` — 135 tests, 135 pass, 0 fail
- `node --import tsx --test src/research-package-http.test.ts` in `services/api` — 29 tests, 29 pass, 0 fail (the import path the second change touches; it failed on `cc407a35`)
- Full `services/api` suite in this worktree — 2476 pass / 8 fail. Every failure is environmental: missing `services/paper/.venv` (the three PDF cases), missing `sciencediscovery_evolve` (the protocol and IdeaTree cases), user namespaces (the Runner case), and the two `API runs ... subagent` cases, which fail the same way on the untouched base `bbdbdd5c`. None of them touches Artifact versions.
- No user-visible surface changes, so no screenshots apply.

Fixes #1300

1312.author: yuanzhou75
1312.body:
Refs #1311

**This addresses the most likely cause of #1311, and it is now verified by execution — but it is not a complete fix for that issue.** Two remaining gaps are listed at the end, so #1311 stays open.

## The problem

`/idea-tree <task>` is deliberately not intercepted: it is sent as an ordinary message, so the agent has to decide by itself to call `create_idea_research` (`apps/desktop/src/idea/command.ts` documents this). The skill that tells it to do that is `skills/idea-tree-team`, and skill selection reads the frontmatter `description`:

```yaml
description: Prepare supplied inputs for autonomous Idea Tree research and explain its saved results.
```

That names no command and contains no literal `/idea-tree`. A message starting with `/idea-tree Skip literature retrieval. Explore low-cost iron catalysts…` therefore contains "Idea Tree" only as a hyphenated command name, while the task subject (catalysts, water treatment) matches `structure-pocket-inspection`, a domain skill in the same catalog. Selection mode is `all` by default (`DEFAULT_SKILL_SELECTION_MODE`, asserted in `services/api/src/selected-skill-defaults.test.ts`), so the right skill is present; it simply was not the one chosen.

## Observed failure

`test/journey-idea-tree-real.spec.ts` on head `a5f028cd`, two runs, same prompt and settings:

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | passed — `1 passed (8.2m)`, model called `create_idea_research` after 72s |
| 2 | failed — 180s card wait expired; the agent was still exploring at round 4 (`list_files` → "Writable workspace is empty" → `$SCIENCEDISCOVERY_SKILLS_DIR/structure-pocket-inspection` → `run_shell` → `Run stopped`) and never called `create_idea_research` |

Ruled out: the sandbox (the same `mkdir` command succeeds standalone) and the selector (run 1 used the identical locator). Tracked as #1311.

## Change

One field, no instruction text:

```yaml
description: "Use when the composer message starts with /idea-tree or /idea-tree-team,
  or the user explicitly asks for autonomous Idea Tree research: prepare supplied
  inputs for the research and explain its saved results."
```

The workflow text below the frontmatter is untouched, and no runtime behaviour changes — only what the selector is told this skill is for.

## Validation — two consecutive passing runs

Head `e4410b801417833e89d24cfba4f189c2e9123881`, same head, two runs of `test/journey-idea-tree-real.spec.ts`, each with its own result directory:

| Run | Exit | Result | Case body | Stack health |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **0** | `1 passed` | 11.3 min (wall 689s) | `200 / status:ok` 10s after start |
| 2 | **0** | `1 passed` | 8.5 min (wall 524s) | `200 / status:ok` 10s after start |

Frontmatter checked independently before running: `yaml.safe_load` on this head's `SKILL.md` returns a dict with keys `['description','name']`, `description` length 207.

**Environment, stated precisely.** `http://127.0.0.1:4310` — default port, and **not an isolated data directory**: the run used the repository default `.sciencediscovery-data`, because `start-stack --mode local` reads the repository `.env`, which overrides an exported `SCIENCE_DISCOVERY_DATA_DIR`. Backend **`legacy`** (`--no-node-build --no-jiuwenswarm`). Model `http://113.46.219.251:8080/v1` with `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`. WSL Ubuntu / linux-amd64. Only `skills/idea-tree-team/SKILL.md` was replaced, and it was restored afterwards.

## The invalid-YAML detour on the previous head

The first version of this change wrote that description **unquoted** (head `667368d7`, blob `bbd0fe23`). It contains `research: prepare` — a colon followed by a space — which in a plain YAML scalar is a mapping indicator, so the frontmatter failed to parse:

```
SKILL.md frontmatter is invalid YAML: Nested mappings are not allowed in
compact mappings at line 2, column 14
```

A skill package that fails to load took the whole API down: every route, `/health` included, answered 400. That is what broke the stack probes, not a probe defect and not isolation behaviour — the same `.env`, port and token answered 200 only once the staged file had been restored, i.e. the two probes were reading different file contents.

Quoting the value makes the colon ordinary text. Verified after the fix: `yaml.safe_load` on this head's frontmatter parses cleanly, so the failure mode is gone at the source. Lesson recorded for anyone editing this field: a `description` containing `": "` must be quoted.

## What #1311 still needs after this

1. **The alternative hypothesis is not excluded.** If selection ignores `description` phrasing and is driven instead by how the prompt orders or presents the selected skill list, this change would not be the cause — two passing runs raise confidence but do not prove the mechanism.
2. **Backend coverage.** All evidence is `legacy`; the daily profile defaults to `jiuwenswarm`. Nothing has been verified there, for this PR or for the journey.

If either needs code, it belongs in #1311's follow-up rather than here.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: none directly — skill selection for `/idea-tree` gains an explicit signal.
Compatibility and migration: none.

1314.author: agent-ci-infra-bot[bot]
1314.body:
A malformed bundled Skill file used to reject startup, and every route — `/health` included — replayed that `SKILL_VALIDATION` as 400. A broken package is now contained to that skill: both built-in loading paths catch validation per package, log it, skip it, keep the rest; `/health` answers 503 while starting or unavailable, and the by-id route answers 404 for a failed bundled id. This revision also resolves the conflict with `main` `d13cead`.

## What changes

1333.body:
An evolve design started with `--no-confirm` could stop on a checkpoint without creating its search, then wait. When checkpoint 2 was not a parseable auto card, the cardless continuation needed the design's pace from the transcript at that instant — but the client's own auto-continue message bumps `sendEpoch`, dropping the previous settle: the pace read as unknown and the continuation returned silently. A dropped-delta stream and a `create_evolve_run` call with no run were silent too; prose checkpoints had no card for the stop badge.

## Changes
- `use-auto-continue.ts`: fall back to the Session's last observed pace while `checkpointMode` is unknown; treat `finalContent` as proof a turn ended; report (and anchor) a notice for endings the client will not push.
- New `EvolveStallNotice`: says the search has not started, prints the exact sentence to send and offers a send button; no card needed. Copy and CSS included.

## Main integration
Rebased onto main (e078fdf). The only conflict was App.tsx's `evolve` prop: main's `EvolveRuns onRetry={...}` is kept and wrapped with `EvolveStallNotice`; main's retry and live-runtime changes are preserved.

## Validation
- `pnpm build`, `pnpm typecheck`, `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs`: ok.
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`: 1559 pass / 0 fail.
- The 28 new tests: 11 fail / 17 pass on main's source, 28 pass with the fix.
- Static render with the app stylesheet at 760/380 px, both locales: no overflow, and the run card sits 26 px below.

## E2E user journeys
BLOCKED: `pnpm ci:ut`, `ci:st`, `ci:e2e` stop at preflight with `BUBBLEWRAP_UNAVAILABLE` (UT 0/8494, ST 0/69, E2E 0/195 executed); the host has no `bwrap` and no root to install it.

Closes #1328

1335.author: nanzhaogang
1335.body: ## Summary The 0.4.0-rc1 account-center acceptance run (Issue #1223) failed on three acceptance criteria and left two P3 observations. This fixes everything that a code change can fix: the ledger's balance column was not additive, a renamed nickname was overwritten on the next sign-in, the seven-day reward strip highlighted the wrong day, the signed-out account panel had no way back and still offered a credits model whose token had just been revoked, and credits printed as `895.877`, which reads as a thousands separator in Chinese. The only reported item left open is D5 (installer not code-signed, Defender firewall prompt); it belongs to the release certificate process, not this repository. Refs #1223 ## The ledger's balance column now continues the ledger `settleCredits` recorded the spendable balance at settle time. That figure already has any second call's hold subtracted from it, while the hold itself has no ledger row, so with two calls in flight the older row dropped by the other call's hold and the next row gained it back — exactly the ±2.227 pair the report found in the 11/20 15:52 batch. The row now continues the previous row's `balance_after`, which makes "previous balance + delta = this balance" hold for every row. Rows and the spendable balance agree again once no hold is open; the top-of-page balance is still the account's own figure, not a second computation. The rule is one helper (`services/accounts/src/ledger.ts`: `ledgerAfter` + `appendLedger`), and **every** writer goes through it — the settle, the sign-in REGISTER/CHECKIN/BONUS rows and the admin adjustment. The previous version fixed only the settle while the grants still wrote `credit_accounts.balance`, so a grant during an open hold broke the chain and the error propagated into every later settle; that is the case zhaozhaozz's P2-1 and the bot's F1 describe. Every writer also takes the `credit_accounts` row (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`) before it inserts. `settleCredits` and `adjustCredits` already did; `signIn` inserted its CHECKIN/BONUS rows before any lock, so under READ COMMITTED a concurrent settle could read an older row, compute a higher id, and leave a pair that is not additive. With the lock taken first, the insert order matches the id order the ledger endpoint returns. ## A saved nickname survives the next sign-in `signIn` wrote `display_name = COALESCE($2, display_name)`, so the HUAWEI profile name the client re-sends on each sign-in replaced whatever the user had saved. The column is now filled only while it is empty (`COALESCE(display_name, $2)`): the first sign-in still seeds the profile name, and a rename survives a sign-out and the next account. Avatar and email keep following the profile. The trade-off is deliberate: once seeded, the column is frozen, so a name changed on the provider side no longer propagates for a user who never renamed here — tracking "user set it" separately would be the way to have both. ## Reward strip, decimals, signed-out panel - `rewardProgress()` derives the strip from the check-in count and whether today is already in the ledger. Four check-ins with today paid now highlights the fourth slot, so the highlight and "3 more days" add up to seven. Before today's sign-in the next claimable day is still the one marked. - The count itself now comes from `GET /v1/me` (`checkins: { total, lastDate }`, counted in SQL), not from the loaded ledger page. The page is capped at 100 rows, so on a busy account today's CHECKIN fell out of it and a paid day rendered as pending (the bot's F4). Older services that do not send `checkins` fall back to the page count, which is what the screenshots below were taken against. - Credits always render with three decimals (`895.877`, `900.000`, `4.123`) alongside the existing thousands grouping. - The signed-out account panel gets a back-to-sessions control, and while no account is signed in the composer withholds the credits model and says why — the provider stays in the catalog, so signing back in needs no setup. ## Validation - `tsc -p apps/desktop/tsconfig.json --noEmit`, `tsc -p services/accounts/tsconfig.json --noEmit`, `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`: clean. - `services/accounts` tests: **45 pass / 0 fail**. `ledger.test.ts` drives the real SQL through a fake `Queryable`, so reverting `appendLedger` to the spendable balance, or `adjustCredits` to an absolute `balance`, fails it (this is the coverage zhaozhaozz's P2-3 and the bot's F3 asked for); the route tests add a grant-while-a-hold-is-open case that asserts both the chain and the final agreement with the page balance, and the existing rename and two-hold cases. - `apps/desktop` tests: **206 tests, 89 pass, 0 fail, 117 skipped** (skips are the `os:linux`-tagged suites, including the new `account-reward-progress` case, which CI runs). - Walked through by hand in the browser, in `zh` and `en`: account page (credits, strip, ledger), sign-out, and the signed-out composer and model picker. Captures below. ## Screenshots The web build of this branch (`apps/desktop/dist`) served by the local control plane, signed in with a HUAWEI account against the production accounts service. The three-decimal credits, the seven-day strip and the signed-out surfaces are rendered by this branch; the client here is the built `apps/desktop` output, not a separately patched page. Ledger rows older than the fix (11/20 15:52) are shown exactly as they are stored — that historical pair is the bot's F2, not something this PR rewrites. **Account page, `zh`** — credits `895.877 / 900.000 / 4.123`; the strip marks days 1–4 done with the fourth as today, and the hint says `再连续 3 天可获满 7 天奖励 +50 积分`; every row's `余额` continues the row below it (`897.262 → 897.249 → 897.226 → 896.138 → 895.877`). **Signed-out account panel, `zh`** — `返回会话` at the top left, and the HUAWEI sign-in button; the panel no longer traps the user. **Signed-out composer, `zh`** — the model pill reads `积分模型需要登录华为账号后才能使用` and the send button is disabled. **Model picker while signed out, `zh`** — only `DeepSeek-V4-Pro` and `添加自定义模型`; the credits provider's models are withheld while no account is signed in. **`en`** — `Back to sessions`, `Sign in with HUAWEI ID to use the credits model`, and a picker listing only `DeepSeek-V4-Pro` and `Add a custom model`. The images live on the throwaway `pr-1335-assets` branch (`pr-assets/1335/`) so the description renders them inline; nothing is added to this PR's tree, and the branch is deleted once this lands. ## E2E user journeys Not run locally: the affected paths need a live accounts service (Postgres, HUAWEI OAuth callback) plus a packaged client, and a second concurrent model call to reproduce the hold interleaving. The desktop changed in the composer and the account page only; no browser journey was added. ## Release Release category: release:fix User impact: the account page's ledger reconciles row by row, a renamed nickname stays, the seven-day strip stops contradicting its own hint, and signing out leaves a usable panel and a model picker that does not offer a dead token. Compatibility and migration: no schema change. Existing ledger rows keep their stored `balance_after`; new rows continue from the latest one, so an old break stays visible in history but does not propagate. `GET /v1/me` gains `checkins: { total, lastDate }`; the desktop treats it as optional, so an older accounts service keeps working with the page-count fallback.

1336.author: qingkwl
1336.body:
## What

Let a macOS installation opt into direct (unsandboxed) local execution — the same installation-level contract Windows already runs — and surface sandbox health in exactly one place: a status row in 设置 › 连接 › 沙箱网络. The opt-in is a switch, off by default; a default install is bit-for-bit unchanged.

The branch carries the feature commit (`6546abbc`), an empty CI-retrigger commit (`7aaf5b2c`, same tree) after a UT flake on the first run (attribution below), a relocation commit (`fe0cff8`) that moves the sandbox opt-in block from 设置 › 通用 to the 沙箱网络 group (user call — see the relocation comment; its diff is moves plus the component split, no copy changes), a map commit (`67bf04d`) that registers the new component in test/source-test-map.json for upstream's changed-path source-test policy (L1 on `fe0cff8` failed on exactly that), a merge of upstream main (`aed6885`) — the map file landed upstream after this branch's base, so the branch merges upstream to keep itself conflict-free; the merge brings no changes of its own — and a round-17 fix commit (`8bfce25`) that splits the double 沙箱网络 heading (the opt-in Group takes 沙箱, the network Group keeps 沙箱网络) and repoints 21 sandbox-related 设置 › 通用 references (including the main.ts:310 support log line) to 设置 › 连接 › 沙箱网络.

## The contract (unchanged doors, one new key)

The Windows contract has two doors: an installation-level opt-in, and a per-run confirmation in pre-flight. This PR ports exactly that to darwin. Nothing about it weakens any door:

- **Per-run confirmation: zero changes.** The whole chain reads the backend value, not the platform — the moment darwin answers `direct`, the existing EvolveCreateDialog banner + confirmation dialog, the `--allow-direct` command write, the read-back check, and the pre-flight refusal (`unisolated_run_unconfirmed`) light up untouched. It covers **evolution candidate runs only**; the Agent's own ephemeral Shell/Python mode under provider `none` is disclosed by the settings status row and governed by the switch (F23 correction on record).
- **Default installs: bit-for-bit unchanged.** `sandboxForPlatform` returns seatbelt exactly as before unless the flag file says `"1"`; regression pins assert both (missing file AND explicit `false`).
- **Fail-closed state hygiene:** the persisted state parses only an exact `"1"` — a truncated or hand-edited file reads OFF; a failed read reads OFF.

## The red lines, addressed head-on

Three comments in the merged code say variations of "darwin never does this", and #1165's acceptance list says "a Seatbelt failure never reaches the main UI… no forward button". This PR is the formal request to retire that line, and the retirement is the product owner's decision, converged over three explicit calls (2026-11-23, recorded in the owner-statement comment on this PR):

1. "沙箱失败不要影响软件运行，最多提示" — a probe failure must not keep the user out of the app. This retires the fail-closed acceptance rule.
2. "不用那么复杂，沙箱失败就失败好了，正常执行，只在用户开启（沙箱相关功能）时提示" — no dedicated banner machinery; the existing EvolveCreateDialog warning + per-run confirmation already tell the user what unsandboxed means, when they actually need to know.
3. "初始化的时候不要拦截沙箱，只在设置那里的沙箱做监测" — the boot flow carries zero sandbox trace; the status row in 设置 › 连接 › 沙箱网络 is the one place sandbox health is surfaced.

**Form A, not Form B.** The rejected alternative was "probe failed → let them in anyway" — zero authorization, silently granted. What this PR implements is the opposite: an **explicit, informed opt-in** the user performs themselves; a probe-failed install runs the stack unsandboxed only until the user says otherwise, with the failure's cause and diagnostics visible on the status row next to the governing switch.

1. `bootstrap.ts` "darwin NEVER sets it": the env pair is injected per-spawn only when the opt-in file says so (or the session's probe failed — same disclosure surface) — same shape as the win32 hard-set, one explicit user action away.
2. `evolution/sandbox.ts` "unavailable → refuse": the opt-in changes what "available" means for that installation (the user's chosen direct mode), matching the documented Windows contract rather than carving out a macOS exception.
3. The fail-closed dead end: the retired page was an MDM-controlled or nested-virtualization first-run user locked out of the app entirely. That UX defect is what this decision removes.

## Where sandbox health lives now (U5c)

- The Seatbelt probe runs at `app.whenReady`, before any flow forks. A failure leaves zero UI trace at boot: log + env + the settings row. The wizard's self-check list is api/runner/model alone.
- 设置 › 连接 › 沙箱网络 gains the status row (green ✓ sandboxed / amber failed with composed cause + diagnostics on the dot tooltip / gray opted-out, names the switch as the way back / neutral-blue attached hedge when the session adopted an already-running backend) and the opt-in switch, hidden by feature-detect on win32/browser.
- The switch's copy carries the full blast radius on the always-visible lead sentence ("With this on, local code execution leaves the sandbox. Applies after a restart." — F29) with the four remaining points behind a「了解完整影响 / Show full impact」`<details>` expander: R execution unavailable, persistent shell/kernel sessions unavailable, evolution runs still confirm each time, restart applies the change.

## Evidence

- `pnpm --dir application test`: **362/362**. `pnpm --dir application typecheck`: clean. api package: 302 cases, 0 fail.
- desktop settings-pages (os-tag lifted locally): 61/61 incl. the `[F29]` pin (clause in `hint`, forbidden in `hintDetails`, both dictionaries) and the six state-row pins; setup-wizard: 7/7.
- **Round-18 frames (head `8bfce25`, the real `NetworkSettings` page)** — captured on the block's current home 设置 › 连接 › 沙箱网络: the 沙箱 Group (status row + opt-in switch) renders above the 沙箱网络 rows, exactly as the page ships. Four zh states (ok / failed+cause / opted-out / attached) + en ok, same harness lineage as rounds 14-15 (real `settings.css`, faked shell bridge, dev-only `settings-shot.dev.tsx` never shipped) — the status dot at the row's right edge, vertically centred (dot-beside), and the hint-split presentation; the zh ok frame shows the lead sentence with the blast radius behind the expander:

| zh ok (green) | zh failed (amber + cause) | zh opted-out (muted) | zh attached (neutral blue) | en ok |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ![18-zh-ok](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/pr-1336-evidence/shots/18-zh-ok.png) | ![18-zh-failed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/pr-1336-evidence/shots/18-zh-failed.png) | ![18-zh-optedout](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/pr-1336-evidence/shots/18-zh-optedout.png) | ![18-zh-attached](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/pr-1336-evidence/shots/18-zh-attached.png) | ![18-en-ok](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/pr-1336-evidence/shots/18-en-ok.png) |

- Round-14 styled set (the same row with the app's real stylesheet, incl. the F26 attached hedge) and the earlier evidence rounds stay in the thread history: [round 14](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/1336#issuecomment-7119401764), [round 15](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/1336#issuecomment-7128117058).
- The F29 copy change itself (round-15 frames predate it by one commit) is pinned by the `[F29]` test, not by a frame.

## CI note (the retrigger commit)

On `6546abbc` the first CI run failed UT at `memory-query-http-forwarding@linux/amd64` — an upstream test (`d13cead9`, after this branch's base) that enters only through the merge preview, failing in its after-hook cleanup (`ENOTEMPTY` rmdir race; the test body passed). The same tree passes on `7aaf5b2c` (18/18). Full attribution in [the flake comment](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/1336#issuecomment-7131789532).

## Non-goals

- No Intel/x64 anything; the flag is darwin-only and inert elsewhere (win32 hard-sets its own env; a plain browser has no bridge).
- No sandbox degrade tier, no "run unsandboxed when Seatbelt is unavailable" automatic behavior of any kind — Form B stays rejected. The automatic part is the session's own mode, never a candidate launch; candidate runs still require `--allow-direct`.
- No second Agent stack; no public API changes (the bridge additions are shell-internal).

1337.body:
A report's `[evidenceN]` chip opened 科学记忆 scoped to the report's Session, and the persisted chip references carried no owning Session. Citing a node created in an earlier Session of the same project therefore always showed "This memory was not found", implying the record was deleted.

## Changes
- Card-side fallback: read the citation's scope first; when nothing matches and the citation names no Session, read once unscoped and use the hit's `sessionId` for provenance. Budget refusals and an unreachable or disabled service stay "unavailable", never "missing".
- The unscoped read is limited to `GLOBALLY_UNIQUE_ID_LABELS` (`Artifact`, `Evidence`, `SourceFile`), whose node id is the record's own key. `DbRecord` is excluded on purpose: its id is the bare `identifier` and the graph keys those nodes by `(session_id, source, identifier)`, so a citation that names no Session returns `unlocated` instead of accepting a same-id record from another Session. The stale "Node ids are globally unique" comment now states this actual semantics.
- A page the sidecar cut short is not proof that nothing exists. `resolveCitation` carries `truncated` out of the scoped and the unscoped read alike and returns the new `unlocated` outcome instead of `missing`; `missing` is now reachable only from a page the sidecar did not cap.
- `memory.notFoundBody` (en/zh) now only says no record matches the citation; an outage keeps its own message, and `unlocated` has its own copy (`memory.unlocatedTitle` / `unlocatedBody`, en/zh) so it never renders the not-found sentence.
- New citations carry the owning Session: the sidecar's `cited_targets`/`chip_map` gain `session_id`, `toChipMap()` copies it, and the report reference persists it. Artifact chips keep none because the artifact dialog resolves them through the project.

## Validation
All numbers below were produced in the task checkout at head `c5ac07e1141e911971859730c8fe9973eb426968` (tree `aa11afc5302aec0f80fd67c2391f9f66524f81f3`), after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`; each names the local log it comes from. The previous description's 1424/1424 figure belonged to the old head `76bf461c` and is not reused here.

- `pnpm build` — exit 0, 41 workspace projects (log: `.tmp/build.log`).
- `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test` — 1435 planned / 1435 executed / 1435 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped, 136 suites (log: `.tmp/desktop-test.log`).
- `pnpm typecheck` — exit 0 (log: `.tmp/typecheck.log`).
- Regression tests against the previous implementation: with only the changed source files restored to `76bf461c` and the new tests kept, the two touched test files give 37 tests / 30 passed / 7 failed, failing exactly on the truncated-page cases (scoped, widened, own-Session, already-unscoped) and the foreign same-id `DbRecord` cases (log: `.tmp/prefix-run.log`).
- Sandboxed layers: `pnpm ci:ut` / `ci:st` / `ci:e2e` still cannot preflight in the task environment — `BUBBLEWRAP_UNAVAILABLE`, no user namespaces, planned 8148/63/189 and executed 0. They are reported as **not run locally**, not as passing; the sandbox-free equivalent is the build + desktop UT + typecheck above, and the containerised layers come from this PR's CI.
- GitHub Actions [run 45170452369](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45170452369) on this head (`c5ac07e1`): `conclusion=success`. Select CI policy, L1, UT, ST, Docker image and Binary release (x86_64/aarch64) succeeded; L4/L5, mocked E2E and the macOS installer are skipped by policy for this change.

## Evidence
Captured in the desktop UI (Chromium 1280×800 CSS viewport at DPR 2) through the desktop E2E mocked control plane. The report lives in `session-1` and cites `[evidence1]`; that Evidence node belongs to another Session, `session-2`. The mock answers the scoped node-type read with no hits and the unscoped read with the node — the shape this fix handles. The capture workspace is tree-identical to `c5ac07e` (`git diff c5ac07e` empty, each changed file hashing the same), so the frames match this head; the capture spec was throwaway and is not committed.

![zh before](https://agent-ci-infra-bot.llmbots.co/pr-media/d8bd03753cc39837aa2f7573ece49a170500d522b5832ad5b0d03e602a3972ff)

1345.author: yuanzhou75
1345.body:
The session-level Idea Tree settings card stored parameters but started nothing, and the research card could go missing. Both are fixed, and the card now works the way the rest of the composer does: it puts a command token in the box instead of acting on it.

## 1. The card offers 确认 / 取消 / 覆盖全局设置, and says what they mean

`apps/desktop/src/views/idea/IdeaTreeOverrideDialog.tsx` drew four actions: 取消, 只用于本次会话, 跟随全局设置, 覆盖全局设置. 跟随全局设置 is gone; the card now draws exactly 确认, 取消 and 覆盖全局设置, and the hint states the contract: confirming applies these values to this conversation, puts the Idea Tree command in the composer, and leaves the global defaults alone; only 覆盖全局设置 writes the defaults.

The undo the removed button provided is visible instead of implicit: every row shows the deployment value it inherits (`全局：5`) and marks the ones this conversation has moved away from (`已覆盖`), so putting a field back to that value and confirming releases the pin — `saveSession`'s empty-diff path writes `{}`, which the Session normalizer reads as no override.

## 2. Confirming seeds the command; the reader sends it

Confirming used to close the card and send the message itself. That made it answer for things it cannot know — a turn already running drops the send without a word, and there was no objective yet — and it made the card the only place the research could start.

It now places `/idea-tree-team` in the composer as the existing blue command token, with the task the reader had already written under it. They complete the task and press send; that send starts the research, and the parameters are read at creation (`services/api/src/idea-tree/research.ts` calls `resolveIdeaTreeSettings(sessionId)`).

- A typed `/idea-tree` keeps its own command in the token, so the token never claims a different command than the one typed.
- A draft that is only a command contributes no task (`ideaTaskOf`), so `/idea-tree-team` followed by 会话设置 can no longer send `/idea-tree-team /idea-tree-team …`.
- A sent token is the confirmed pass: `sendMessage` composes the token and the task and never defers back into the card.
- With nothing written the token cannot be sent at all: the composer's send button and Enter both require a task, so the reader writes the question before anything leaves the box. The box asks for one in the token's own words.

## 3. Confirming is refused when it could not write

From the settings row the confirm is also the write, so it is offered only with a conversation open and a draft that was actually read: no Session, or a failed settings read, leaves 确认 disabled rather than placing a token that would run on the deployment values while the hint promises "these values". A command the reader typed still comes back to them as a token even when the read failed — that path writes nothing by design.

## 4. The research card no longer goes missing

`idea_research.created` sat in the run-stream reducer's deferred list, so the desktop ignored it. The list was only re-read while the command's five-minute waiting window was open, and a real model spends that long on preparation before it calls `create_idea_research` — after which nothing re-read the list and the card at the transcript's foot never appeared. The event is now counted (`run-stream/model.ts`, `reducer.ts`) and the app re-reads the list when it arrives, the same way `evolve_run.created` already did.

## 5. Documentation matches the card again

Both `docs/{zh,en}/developer-docs/desktop-frontend.md` described 只用于本次会话 and 跟随全局设置 → `null`. They now describe the three actions, the inherited-value rows, the release-by-reverting path, and the token the confirm seeds.

## Screenshots

Component-level renders of the repository's own `IdeaTreeOverrideDialog` and `Composer` with the app's own stylesheet, driven by stub clients — not the full application journey, and the Electron window is not automated in this environment.

- before = `77b3a93883408c84dc11205f3f0f9553fc4c3068` (main), after = `4f64d464cc7e89b8f1f4859e78944d68facc2e76`

1361.author: zhaozhaozz
1361.body:
## Summary

1. Routes only **merge queue (`merge_group`)** runs of **`UT`** and the three heavy **L2 mocked E2E shards (`standard-config`, `standard-journeys`, `research`)** to self-hosted Docker runners (`[self-hosted, Linux, X64, sciencediscovery]`), gated behind the repository variable `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE == 'true'` (default off).
2. Enables **in-runner 2-stack local parallelism (`CI_E2E_LOCAL_CONCURRENCY=2`)** for the two long standard mocked E2E shards (`standard-config` and `standard-journeys`) so each job runs two fully isolated local stacks in parallel (disjoint loopback ports, runtime directories, `JIUWENSWARM_HOME` roots, desktop Vite port/cache directories, and Playwright `workers: 1`), cutting L2 end-to-end wall time roughly in half on both self-hosted and GitHub-hosted runners.

Closes #1360

## Motivation

In merge-queue runs, `UT` (~13 min) and the three heavy L2 mocked E2E shards (`standard-config` ~20 min, `standard-journeys` ~20 min plus ~3.5 min queued behind `max-parallel: 4`, `research` ~10 min) dominate wall-clock time before `L3 real E2E` can start. Moving those four trusted merge-queue jobs onto dedicated Dockerized self-hosted runners with container-local caches and running 2 isolated stacks inside each of the two long standard shards brings all four jobs into a ~9–12 min band without exposing self-hosted runners to untrusted `pull_request` (or fork) runs or splitting any spec file.

## Changes

### Merge-queue self-hosted routing & container-local cache
- **`.ci/tier-policy.mjs`**:
  - Export `SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER = ['self-hosted', 'Linux', 'X64', 'sciencediscovery']`.
  - Compute `self_hosted_merge_queue = event === 'merge_group' && selfHostedMergeQueue === true` and `ut_runner` (`SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER` when enabled, otherwise `'ubuntu-latest'`). Non-`merge_group` events (`pull_request`, `workflow_dispatch`, `workflow_call`, `schedule`, `push`) always fail closed to `'ubuntu-latest'`.
- **`.ci/mocked-matrix.mjs`**:
  - Export `HEAVY_MOCKED_SHARDS` (`standard-config`, `standard-journeys`, `research`) and `buildMockedMatrix()`.
  - Emit `runner`, `self_hosted`, and `local_concurrency` (`2` for `standard-config`/`standard-journeys`, `1` for `research`/`governed`/`literature`) per shard.
- **`.ci/use-local-swarm-cache.sh`**:
  - Manage a `flock`-serialized, content-hashed read-only JiuwenSwarm installation under `${SD_CI_CACHE_DIR:-/ci-cache}/jiuwenswarm/<key>/src`.
  - Strip `.git` and pre-install `pytest>=8.3.5` (for `check:swarm-contract`) while holding the lock so concurrent UT/E2E jobs never mutate the shared venv and `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup` takes its pre-installed read-only fast path while every job keeps its own isolated `JIUWENSWARM_HOME` under `CI_RUNTIME_DIR`.
  - Export only `JIUWENSWARM_SRC` to `$GITHUB_ENV`.
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**:
  - Wire `vars.CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE` through `policy` -> `e2e-plan` / `ut` / `e2e`.
  - Raise mocked `e2e` `max-parallel` from `4` to `5` and pass `CI_E2E_LOCAL_CONCURRENCY: ${{ matrix.local_concurrency }}`.
  - Skip cross-region `actions/cache` round trips (pnpm, uv, Playwright Chromium, JiuwenSwarm) only when a job is routed to a self-hosted runner, replacing JiuwenSwarm cache restore with `.ci/use-local-swarm-cache.sh`.
  - Make `Provision the bubblewrap sandbox` idempotent in `ut` and `e2e` by probing `bwrap --unshare-user --ro-bind / / --dev /dev true` before invoking `sudo apt-get` / `sudo sysctl`.
- **`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`**:
  - Export `sharedCacheEnv()` and honor pre-set `UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR`, `npm_config_cache`, and `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` (matching existing `UV_CACHE_DIR` handling) while preserving exact workspace-local fallbacks when unset.

### In-runner 2-stack local parallelism (`standard-config` & `standard-journeys`)
- **`test/support/tagged/execution.mjs`**:
  - Export `PARALLEL_MOCKED_SHARDS`, `mockedLocalConcurrency()`, `splitEntriesByFile()`, `mockedExecutionLanes()`, and `mockedSlotEnvironment()`.
  - Balance whole spec files across 2 lanes (never splitting a spec file across stacks); for `standard-config`, keep `mocked-standard-config-fresh` in its own pristine stack and keep the 9 JiuwenSwarm supplemental checks exclusively on `mocked-standard-config-global`. Single-file PR selections and non-standard shards (`research`, `governed`, `literature`) remain single-stack.
- **`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`**:
  - Execute `mockedExecutionLanes()` concurrently via `Promise.all` with disjoint loopback port blocks (`4410`/`4420`, `4411`/`4421`, `4510`/`4520`, `17774`/`17784`, desktop Vite `4178`/`4179`), separate `CI_RUNTIME_DIR`, `JIUWENSWARM_HOME`, and Vite cache dirs. Default remains `1` (serial) for local `pnpm ci:e2e`.
- **`.ci/run-e2e.sh`**:
  - Serialize JiuwenSwarm port allocation across concurrent local stacks via `CI_E2E_SWARM_START_LOCK` (`flock`), explicitly closing fd 8 (`8>&-`) on child commands so daemonized processes never inherit the lock descriptor; avoid redundant `ln -sfn` rewrites on `test/node_modules`.
- **`test/helpers/desktop-evolve.ts` & `apps/desktop/vite.config.ts`**:
  - Honor `E2E_DESKTOP_PORT` (default `4178`) and `E2E_DESKTOP_VITE_CACHE_DIR` so concurrent desktop-entry specs never collide on Vite port or `.vite` cache.
- **`.ci/mocked-report.mjs`**:
  - Audit all `mocked-*` sub-lane directories in shard artifacts so any unexpected `jiuwenswarm-checks.json` outside the single designated check batch fails with `UNEXPECTED_SWARM_CHECKS`.
- **`.ci/README.md`, `.ci/mocked-shards.test.mjs`, `.ci/self-hosted-merge-queue.test.mjs`**:
  - Document the toggle, `max-parallel: 5`, and `CI_E2E_LOCAL_CONCURRENCY=2`, and add unit, CLI, workflow contract, reconciliation, and hermetic shell tests.

## Safety & Rollout

- **Default off for self-hosted routing**: While `vars.CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE` is unset, all PR and merge-queue jobs stay on `ubuntu-latest`. Clearing or changing the variable rolls back immediately with no workflow edit.
- **Event boundary**: `pull_request` (including forks), `workflow_dispatch`, `schedule`, `push`, light mocked shards (`governed`, `literature`), `ST`, desktop jobs, packaging, and real E2E jobs never route to self-hosted runners even when `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE=true`.
- **Strong isolation**: Each local E2E lane runs its own isolated service stack and Playwright `workers: 1`; `CI_E2E_LOCAL_CONCURRENCY=1` reverts any run to serial execution.

## Verification

### Local static & unit checks
- `node --test .ci/self-hosted-merge-queue.test.mjs`: **8/8 passed** (0 failed, 0 skipped)
- `node --test .ci/*.test.mjs`: **228/228 passed** (0 failed, 0 skipped)
- `bash -n .ci/run-e2e.sh`, `bash -n .ci/use-local-swarm-cache.sh`, YAML validation on `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: **passed**
- `node .ci/test-selector.mjs check`: **passed** (11 cases, 20 tags, 4 layers)
- `node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs`: **passed** (143 Markdown files checked)
- `node scripts/check-architecture.mjs`: **passed** (392 package source files checked)
- `CI_ENFORCE_SOURCE_MAP=1 node .ci/changed-path-check.mjs`: **passed** (0/0 mapped)
- `node test/check-e2e-meta.mjs`: **passed** (127 spec files, 0 errors)

### Full 4-way concurrent self-hosted Docker benchmark (`bc801d94d`, 16 vCPU / 60.6 GiB host)
All 4 target merge-queue jobs executed concurrently in isolated `sd-actions-runner:local` containers with `CI_E2E_LOCAL_CONCURRENCY=2` on `standard-config` and `standard-journeys`:
- **`UT`** (`merge` + `--coverage`): **8345/8345 passed** in **561s (9m21s)**
- **`L2 E2E (research)`** (1 stack): **21/21 passed** in **554s (9m14s)**
- **`L2 E2E (standard-journeys)`** (2 stacks: 44 + 44): **88/88 passed** in **674s (11m14s)** (down from 17m44s single-stack / ~23m48s GitHub Actions incl. queue)
- **`L2 E2E (standard-config)`** (2 stacks: 32 + 9 Swarm checks, 4 fresh + 37 global): **73/73 passed + 9/9 JiuwenSwarm checks passed** in **735s (12m15s)** (down from 17m29s single-stack / 20m10s GitHub Actions)
- **Host resource profile (4-container concurrent window)**: CPU avg **60.4%** (9.67 / 16 vCPU, P95 80.6%), RAM peak **15.18 GiB / 60.6 GiB** (25%, 45.4 GiB free).

Release category: `release:internal`

内容宽度与设置页一致（最大 1120px 并居中），不再横向铺满窗口。 - 积分概览改为「可用 + 已消耗 = 累计获得」：三个数字由同一份 milli-credit 数据推导，任意时刻都能对上（此前「累计获得」取整、「累计消耗」取服务端字段，二者与余额可能不相等）。 - 积分流水最多读取/展示 1000 条，并在末页提示「仅显示最近 1000 条流水，更早的记录不再列出。」 - 修复个人中心每隔数秒被重新加载的问题：加载只依赖访问令牌，回调改走 ref，不再随工作区刷新抖动。 **3. 退出与未登录态** - 新增单元测试：流水按类裁剪的 SQL 形状、昵称不被华为资料覆盖、积分合计恒等；签到独立表的计数与奖励周期当前由 e2e 覆盖，store 级回归测试列为后续项。 ## 修改前后截图 左列为修改前（父提交 `d13cead9`），右列为修改后（本 PR）。截图在 Windows、1600×1000 视口下渲染，接口使用 e2e 的确定性 mock 数据，不含真实账号信息。 ### 1. 账号登录入口 | 修改前 | 修改后 | | --- | --- | | | | ### 2. 自定义模型配置 | 修改前 | 修改后 | | --- | --- | | | | ### 3. 个人中心 | 修改前 | 修改后 | | --- | --- | | | | ### 4. 积分流水上限 | 修改前 | 修改后 | | --- | --- | | | | ### 5. 退出华为账号 | 修改前 | 修改后 | | --- | --- | | | | ### 6. 设置 › 模型（未登录） | 修改前 | 修改后 | | --- | --- | | | | ### 7. 华为登录回跳落地 | 修改前 | 修改后 | | --- | --- | | | | ## 验证 - **账本裁剪**：earned 侧条件改为 `delta >= 0`，零增量行同样受 1000 行上限约束；`ledger.test.ts` 同步断言。 - **签到 streak**：新签到写入真实连续天数；历史回填行保留 0（旧账本无法还原连续天数）。该列当前不展示给用户。 ## 支持口径 - 账户累计获得/消耗以 `credit_accounts.total_earned / total_spent` 为准，签到与七日周期以 `checkins` 表为准；账本行只是展示凭据，earned 侧裁剪旧凭据不影响余额与周期。 - 1364.author: yuanzhou75
1364.body:
The nightly L4 case `test/journey-idea-tree-real.spec.ts` failed intermittently, for three separate reasons that looked identical from the assertion. Each is fixed where it belongs, and once they were fixed the remaining reds turned out to be the case's own wall-clock budgets.

## 1. A research could exist and never be drawn (product bug)

`apps/web/src/IdeaResearchCard.tsx` read the list once on mount and refreshed only when `idea_research.created` arrived on the run stream. That event is not replayed, so a client that attached late, reloaded or reconnected never learned the research existed: it was there, the Session had it, and the card was never drawn.

The card now re-reads the list while a research may be on its way, and stops as soon as one appears:

- **Anchor.** Two moments live in refs — the list coming back empty, and an *expectation* — and the later one wins, so a Session that has been open for hours still gets a window when the command is sent.
- **Expectation.** The composer announces it when it accepts an `/idea-tree` command (`armIdeaResearchCard`); `refreshSession` announces it when the client attaches to a run it was not watching (`announceAttachedRun`, on a replayed `idea_research.created` or on an active run, because the replay may no longer carry the event).
- **Replay.** The replayed created event is now used instead of dropped: `resumeSessionRun` subscribes *after* the last replayed sequence, which is exactly why the card never heard it.
- **Bound.** Ten minutes — the case's `CREATE_BUDGET_MS` is 600s and one measured run created its research at 403s — at 5s for the first two minutes and 30s after that. The chain ends when the window is spent, and an expectation is spent as soon as the list grows past the count it had when it was announced, so a drawn research costs no further reads.
- **A list that is not empty is no longer skipped**, so a second research whose created event was missed in a Session that already holds one is drawn as well.

## 2. The journey asked the interface before the fact

It waited for the card first, so "the command started nothing" and "the card did not draw it" produced the same red. It now polls the API for exactly one new research, takes its id, and only then waits 60s for the card. A research that never settles reports its last status, phase, round, tokens and `reason`; a run that ends `failed`, `blocked` or `cancelled` before a research exists fails at once, naming that run's status and reason.

## 3. A headless run could be stopped by an approval card

Measured on the live stack: the run went `running` → **`blocked`** after 40s, `research_items` stayed empty, and the timeout then cancelled the run. `createProjectAndSession` was called without `approvalMode`, while every other real journey on this stack passes `always_allow`. The journey now asks for the same mode.

## 4. The remaining reds were the case's caps, not the product

With the three causes above fixed, two runs on the previous head still failed on their budgets:

| run | wall | what happened |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 788s | research created at 77s, then model calls of 45-130s each; at the 720s terminal cap it was in `aggregate` round 2 and had just finished a call — slow, not stalled |
| 2 | 314s | no research inside 300s while the run was `running`; it appeared at **403s** |

A live model's latency is not something the product can fail, but a stall is. The waits are bounded by progress:

- creating: up to 600s, and at once when the run ends `failed`/`blocked`/`cancelled`;
- settling: up to 1800s, and at once after 15 minutes without a new token, round, activity or node — the same allowance the real shard gives a research turn (`.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml:122-123`: `SCIENCE_AGENT_GATEWAY_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS: '900000'`, "Allow long research turns to go up to fifteen minutes without progress"). One provider call advances none of those counters, so a shorter threshold would report provider latency as a stall;
- case budget 3000s.

## Runs on a live stack

Isolated stack, real model `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`, every run triggered with `npm --prefix .e2e run test:real -- journey-idea-tree-real.spec.ts`; a run the harness reports as BLOCKED (stack unreachable, Playwright exits 0) is retried and never counted.

| # | head | verdict | wall |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `8a38dfaa` | pass | 1412s |
| 2 | `8a38dfaa` | pass | 801s |
| 3 | `8a38dfaa` | pass | 961s |
| 4 | `8a38dfaa` | pass | 814s |
| 5 | `8a38dfaa` | pass | 640s |
| 6 | `6397aeac` | pass | 865s |
| 7 | `6397aeac` | pass | 745s |
| 8 | `6397aeac` | pass | 797s |
| 9 | `7a5e3999` | pass | 1058s |
| 10 | `7a5e3999` | pass | 580s |
| 11 | `7a5e3999` | pass | 582s |

**5 / 5 pass** on `8a38dfaa`. The first of those runs is the one that used to fail: its research appeared 399s after the command and needed 23 minutes of engine work to settle — inside the progress-bounded waits, past the old 720s cap.

**3 / 3 pass** on head `6397aeac` (2026-11-25 17:08–17:48 local, back to back, no retries). The tree was `main` at `77b3a938` with that head's six files overlaid, each checked against its blob id before the build (`spec` `8c3ea3b6`, card `3b86699c`). The third run's journey report: 65.1s to start the research, 726.5s to reach a terminal status, 734ms to confirm the reload still returns it.

Those six files are byte-identical at the current head: the branch is now rebased onto `main` with no merge commit, and `git diff 6397aeac 7a5e3999` over the six paths is empty, so the runs describe the code as it stands. The rebase also carries the one change made since the runs — the `test/source-test-map.json` entry for `apps/web/src/ideaResearchNotice.ts` that L1 requires.

**3 / 3 pass on the final head `7a5e3999`** (independent repeat, 2026-11-25 20:02–20:39 local): tree = `main` at `9c74af8b` plus this head's seven files, blob ids re-checked before and after every run and unchanged. No run was BLOCKED and none was retried. The third run's journey report: 77.1s to start the research, 500.0s to a terminal status, 823ms for the reload; the first two runs' step timings were overwritten by the shared report path, so only their wall clocks are quoted. The spread between them (1058s against 580s) sits in the settling tail, the same shape as the earlier group.

## Screenshots

Component-level renders of the repository's own `IdeaResearchCard` with the app's stylesheet, driven by a stub client whose list is empty at mount and returns a research on the second timer beat. **No `idea_research.created` event is dispatched at any point** — the card is drawn by its own timer, which is the fix. Not the full application journey; the harness note above each frame says so.

Pinned to the storage commit `06fced089e961b676a4ccafee52740a29637382a` (`shots/idea-tree-card/`):

| zh-CN | en |
|---|---|
| ![card zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/06fced089e961b676a4ccafee52740a29637382a/shots/idea-tree-card/card-zh.png) | ![card en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/06fced089e961b676a4ccafee52740a29637382a/shots/idea-tree-card/card-en.png) |

## Tests

- `apps/web` suite: **1400 pass / 0 fail** — five mounted cases for the card (appears with no created event; the cadence slows and the chain stops; a fresh callback identity every render cannot restart the window; a command sent into a long-open Session opens a new window and the expectation ends once its research is drawn; a second research is drawn in a Session that already holds one) and four for the helpers (a replayed created event arms; an active run arms; an ordinary refresh does not; only an `/idea-tree` command counts).
- `test/check-e2e-meta.mjs`: 127 spec files, 0 errors.
- `tsc -p apps/web/tsconfig.json --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`: clean.

## Scope

The L4 journey itself was run repeatedly against a real isolated stack and a live model; the frames above are component renders, not the full app journey, and the Electron window is not automated in this environment.

1367.body:
Running the release profile from the general CI entry point can share its concurrency group with other CI runs. The Release workflow can now be dispatched on demand and runs the same L5 test plan, including UT/ST coverage reporting, without requiring a release tag.

## Release gate

- Add manual dispatch to Release, using the selected ref's application version to stamp build artifacts. Pass through the backend and worker limit to the existing reusable CI workflow.
- Give L5 runs a concurrency group per workflow, ref, and event. Keep an in-progress L5 run from being cancelled by a later run in its group.
- Collect and report UT/ST coverage from both manual entry points. A version tag push runs L5 with coverage disabled and still creates the draft Release after a successful gate.

## Validation

| Check | Planned | Executed | Passed | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Local `pnpm ci:l1` | 4 | 4 | 4 | Passed |
| Local CI self-tests (`node --test .ci/*.test.mjs`) | 222 | 222 | 222 | Passed |
| GitHub PR gate L1 | 4 | 4 | 4 | Passed |
| GitHub PR gate UT | 8,368 | 8,368 | 8,368 | Passed |
| GitHub PR gate ST | 69 | 69 | 69 | Passed |
| GitHub PR gate mocked E2E | 6 | 6 | 6 | Passed across both shards |

`actionlint` passed on the original head before the documentation-only follow-up. On `53a81ad2`, GitHub Actions passed Coverage, both Linux binary builds, Docker, and `merge-gate`. CodeCheck and CLA also passed. The full L5 suite is outside the PR profile.

[GitHub Actions run 45421640225](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45421640225)

## E2E user journeys

**Product E2E: not applicable.** This change only affects GitHub Actions entry points and coverage artifacts. The workflow contract tests cover L5 concurrency and the manual versus tag-triggered paths.

## Release

Release category: `release:internal`

User impact: Release maintainers can run the L5 gate manually and inspect its coverage report. The application is unaffected.

Compatibility and migration: None.

Fixes #1352.

`health()` trusted only the unauthenticated `/health`, so a token mismatch kept Settings at `运行正常` while every query answered `401`. The old by-node-type probe scanned the graph, whose 503 budget refusal read as "Cannot connect". The probe is now O(1), with a mixed-version fallback.

## Changes
- Sidecar `GET /internal/ping` (Bearer) returns `{status:"ok"}` without touching graph data.
- `health()` reads `/health`, then pings: 401/403 → unauthorized; 404/405 (older sidecar) re-checks with the authenticated by-node-type read; a known `memory_graph_query_limit` refusal keeps `/health`; any other failure → degraded.
- Query, subgraph, web-page-hash and search reads map 401/403 to `memory_graph_unauthorized`; the web-page content route keeps every failure reason a 502. Settings and card/provenance show `凭据被拒绝` / "Credentials rejected".
- Provenance review treats that reason as inconclusive.

- sidecar ping/health 2/2; full file 115 pass, 78 live-Neo4j fixture errors unchanged. CodeCheck: GitHub check 0 annotations; GitCode needs credentials; this push re-triggers it.

- desktop 1470/1470; typechecks clean.

A `necessary` export materialised every run event and then walked the same streams again for the trajectory; CAS sizing streamed (and hashed twice) payloads whose length was already in metadata. The dialog re-walked the session tree repeatedly, and an export task walked it twice.

## What changed
- `necessary` no longer calls `exportRunStreams`. Its omitted-event count reuses the trajectory walk and counts only streams that walk did not open, so it matches `complete` exactly for orphan tool streams and legacy main arrays. The builder-only count is stripped before records are written.
- Added `ContentStore.storedSize` for preview sizing. It declines ambiguous multi-layout objects; the preview then uses a verified read so it sizes the same intact copy the writer emits. The writer still verifies every object.
- A panel request now takes one revision snapshot: `watch` only registers, `defaults` builds. The build reports when its own reconcile wrote provenance; only then does the request take a second walk, adopt it and retry. Cache entries are published under the final revision, and queued profiles remove pre-adoption keys on both success and ready paths.
- Added `research-package.stage` timing for route preflight, enumerate, records, trajectory, summarize, CAS sizing and write.

## Measured performance
Committed script `scripts/measure-research-package-export.mjs`, run as `node --import tsx scripts/measure-research-package-export.mjs --events <N> --cas-bytes <B> --rounds 5`. One warm-up, median of 5 rounds, baseline `e61b1d29` detached worktree vs this head on the same host. The reporter's 189 KB/1.8 GB data is unavailable, so this is a synthetic fixture: 1 session, 1 completed run, 0 workspace files, 3 referenced CAS objects (50% code, 25% stdout, 25% stderr).

| Fixture | preview | export build+write | exportRunStreams | cas.stream (preview) | revision walks | omitted = complete |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 500k events, 1 MiB CAS | 2682 → 1573 ms | 2841 → 1526 ms | 1 → 0 | 3 calls / 1,048,576 B → 0 / 0 | 11 → 1 | 500000 = 500000 |
| 200k events, 112 MiB CAS | 1349 → 657 ms | 1783 → 1325 ms | 1 → 0 | 3 calls / 117,440,512 B → 0 / 0 | 11 → 1 | 200000 = 200000 |

Export `cas.stream` stays 6 calls (hash + write) in both, because the writer still verifies. Packages stayed ~4.3 KB and ~117.4 KB. The earlier "up to 15 walks" was inferred from the code (3 per profile); the measured baseline for the five-profile request is 11, and this head is 1.

## Validation
- Local: `pnpm typecheck`; CAS 60 pass / 2 skipped; research preview/necessary/export/listing/replay/store/trajectory 184 pass; `research-package-http` 29 pass; full API 2514 pass / 9 fail / 2 skipped (unrelated: six need bubblewrap, one dirty-worktree guard, two model.usage assertions reproduce on baseline); `pnpm ci:selftest` 220 pass, `pnpm docs:lint` clean, `pnpm architecture:check` 121 pass plus one unrelated jiuwenswarm relative-path assertion.

- Local tagged UT/ST/E2E are BLOCKED at preflight `BUBBLEWRAP_UNAVAILABLE` (bwrap absent, non-root); the GitHub layers above ran them.

## E2E user journeys
Passed in GitHub Actions: L2 E2E (mocked, standard-config) and L2 E2E (mocked, standard-journeys). Locally the tagged layer is BLOCKED by the missing bwrap preflight, so no local journey ran.

## Release
Release category: release:performance
User impact: the export dialog and necessary package build no longer pay for the full run history twice.
Compatibility and migration: none; the package format and omitted-count semantics are unchanged.

## Remaining risk
`sessionTrajectory` still makes one index pass over run events, so the work stays linear in that pass but no longer repeats `exportRunStreams`. A preview that writes workspace provenance takes the documented second walk, and each queued profile re-checks `canWarm` (11 probes in the five-profile test). An external evidence change during a build returns that request's snapshot; the next poll recalculates, and export is still stopped by its post-write revision check.

1374.body:
Turns the millisecond instrumentation the shell, start-stack and jiuwenswarm already emit into a two-layer timing budget gate, mirroring the pyc-budget pattern (pure functions + tests pinning the REAL measured numbers).

Design doc: mac-design perf-guard design P1 (issue #1165 follow-up: "Release CI policy" acceptance item).

## What changes

Six pure additions, no runtime behavior change:

- `application/scripts/lib/parse-perf-timeline.mjs`: parses shell.log perf lines (timestamped relay lines, bare pipe-flush lines, multi-word shell events, warmup 200). Splits sessions at module-load; detects session kind (first/warm) from the provisioning flag. Component durations are event-PAIR values that respect clock domains: same-domain pairs subtract domain-local offsets, cross-domain pairs (api-spawn->HEALTH-200, AGENT-READY->warmup) use the ISO wall clock.
- `application/scripts/lib/perf-verdict.mjs`: three verdicts - ok / hang (over hangMs or a missing pair: the ready/healthy event never arriving IS the hang signal) / regression (over baseline x 1.4, warn-first, 2-strike hard fail upstream). First and warm sessions get separate budget tables (the unpack tax only exists in first sessions).
- `application/scripts/perf-budget.json`: single source of truth for budgets (H1-H9 hang / R1-R12 baselines from the design doc). Baselines measured on the 2026-11-24 three-session log of the signed v0.4.0 build (first 18.8s / warm 8.5s & 8.2s to AGENT-READY); agent-ready hangMs equals AGENT_READY_TIMEOUT_MS so the gate and the runtime timeout blow together.
- `application/scripts/perf-gate.mjs`: the CLI entry the build smoke step (build-mac.sh step 6, future P3) will call. Exit 0 (ok / regression-warn) / 1 (hang) / 2 (usage). Flags: --json, --fail-on-regression (release runs and the two-strike counter).
- `application/scripts/README-perf-budget.md`: maintainer docs - quick start, mechanism, verdict rules, budget-editing discipline, honest known-limits list.
- `application/test/perf-budget.test.ts`: 21 tests. Fixtures pin the REAL 2026-11-24 measured values (any parser change that stops extracting them turns red by name); W25-shaped inputs (missing-healthy, 2x regression) must NOT pass; fool-proofing: hang lines must sit above regression lines, tolerance locked to the 1.2-2.0 band, every budgeted component must exist in the parser's pair table.

## Impact to review

None at runtime: the gate is read-only over logs, never mutates them, and is not yet wired into any build step. Wiring into build-mac.sh step 6 is the follow-up (P3), gated on owner sign-off of the budget values.

## Validation

- `node --experimental-strip-types --no-warnings --test test/perf-budget.test.ts`: 21/21 pass.
- End-to-end on the real 2026-11-24 shell.log: 3 sessions (1 first + 2 warm) all ok, exit 0.
- JSON output machine-verified; usage-error paths exit 2.
- No runtime / product code changed: pure additions, gate runs read-only.

## E2E user journeys

Not applicable: no app behavior changes. The gate consumes existing logs only.

## Release

Release category: release:internal
User impact: None. CI/build tooling only.
Compatibility and migration: Additive only; the gate activates when build-mac.sh step 6 wires it (separate PR, P3).


## Linked issues

- **Relates to #1165** — the macOS desktop adaptation tracker. This PR is the follow-up to its **"Release CI policy"** acceptance item: it adds the machine-checked macOS timing gate (the `macos-desktop` CI job now smoke-launches the packed `.app` and judges the first-run `shell.log` against `perf-budget.json` in `--hang-only` mode, uploading the measured log as an artifact). The concrete v1 policy answer: manual real-Mac evidence stays the baseline source; the CI gate covers the silent-hang class on every PR/push. Evidence summary posted on the issue.
- P2 (wizard/reuse-path instrumentation) and P3-2 (baseline collection from release-run logs, per `README-perf-budget.md` rule 2) remain follow-ups by design.

## Status after merge

Merged as `9c74af8b` (2026-11-25). The body above describes the first review round; final merged state: 11 commits, **19 findings (F1-F19) resolved across 8 review rounds**, **33/33 tests** green, and the CI wiring (`ci.yml` `macos-desktop` smoke + log-artifact upload, shown in the files tab) is **included in this PR** — verified green end-to-end on a real macOS runner before merge (fork Package@macos run 45541198600: ok 10 / hang 0 / exit 0).

1379.body:
Packaged macOS first runs re-point `<dataDir>/envs/*/bin/python*` at the bundled interpreter with a relative symlink computed by `posix.relative`. When the data dir arrives in a symlinked spelling (`/tmp`, `/var`) while `resourcesPath` is the resolved spelling (`/private/tmp`, `/private/var`), the two strings share no textual prefix, `relative()` counts the shorter textual depth, and the link lands one directory short (`/private/private/...`) — the stack then fail-fasts with `SHARED_ENV is missing` (#1374 saw this live).

## Change
- `application/src/bootstrap.ts`: the darwin `fixVenvLaunchers` branch computes the hop target from `realpathOrSelf(venvBinDir)` and `join(realpathOrSelf(<python>/bin), "python3")`. The new `realpathOrSelf` helper falls back to the given spelling when realpath cannot resolve a side, so first run never throws. The target remains relative, preserving the relocation property W17 exists for.
- The realpath-based idempotence gate is unchanged, so an install already carrying the broken target is rewritten on its next launch (the short-circuit path always re-runs this fix). The new test's second phase proves that self-heal.

## Validation
- `cd application && node --experimental-strip-types --no-warnings --test test/*.test.ts`: 363 tests, 361 pass, 0 fail, 2 skipped (win32/darwin-only process-tree tests).
- New POSIX-gated test: alias-spelled data dir under a symlink that adds a component, platform `darwin`; fails on the unpatched code (`python must resolve`), passes with the fix. It also asserts via `readlink` that each written target — first run and healed — stays relative (`posix.isAbsolute` false); an absolute-target mutation fails it with `python target must stay relative`. A second phase stores the old textual target with a valid stamp and asserts the relaunch heals all three links.
- `cd application && pnpm typecheck`: clean.
- Where the test runs: `application/test` is not collected by the Linux ut layer; `pnpm --dir application test` runs in the windows-desktop job (this POSIX case skips there) and on macOS via `application/scripts/build-mac.sh`. The existing W17 darwin cases are macOS-gated and did not run here; their fixtures are untouched.

## E2E user journeys
BLOCKED: requires a packaged macOS `.app`, unavailable in this environment. The regression is exercised through the real `bootstrapPackaged` entry point with the darwin platform argument in the POSIX test above.

## Release
Release category: release:fix
User impact: packaged macOS first runs, and relaunches of affected installs, no longer leave dangling venv launchers.
Compatibility and migration: none; affected installs self-heal on the next launch.

Closes #1376

```
cd application && node --experimental-strip-types --no-warnings --test test/*.test.ts
```

The MCP list switch previously changed session-default selection, while the edit form changed service enablement. A server could therefore look switched on in the list and still be disabled in its configuration.

1386.author: zhaochen39
1386.body:
Eight edge cases can lose data during recovery, cause inconsistent research state, or change how the desktop and web apps present results. This change adds focused regression coverage for each case.

## Persistence and run history

- Repair the local graph journal tail before new records are appended. A torn final record is truncated, including invalid partial UTF-8. A valid final record without a newline is kept and terminated so the next append stays separate.
- Skip malformed run-stream JSONL records during replay. Require a non-negative safe integer sequence, a string timestamp, and an event object with a string type.

## Tool execution and context

- Propagate parallel tool rejections with `undefined` or `null` after draining in-flight calls, and stop scheduling new calls. Register both regression cases with literal titles so the tagged UT collector can discover them.
- Reject sparse arrays with an error identifying the missing index. Explicit `null` entries remain valid.

## Desktop and web

- Preserve literal comparisons in paper titles and abstracts. Remove common HTML and JATS inline and structural tags, handle escaped tags with quoted attributes, and split escaped blocks into paragraphs.
- Keep CSV artifact row keys unique even when generated IDs would collide with explicit IDs that appear later in the import.
- Keep the latest Idea Research snapshot when a list response races a stream update, so paused research stays paused and the Continue button remains available.

## Account check-ins

- Validate the daily reward and streak settings at startup and document the accepted environment variable format. Keep the existing defaults and legacy bonus-period setting.

## Validation

- On `c17479d718765c219bba22c3f279e320cfaeec85`, 70 focused checks passed in review: 19 desktop paper-text, 48 web CSV, and 3 Idea Research card tests. The new regression test delays the list response until after the stream reports `paused` and verifies that the Continue button remains available.
- GitHub Actions passed L1, UT, ST, and the [merge gate](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45585984445/job/139122562993) on this head.
- Before rebasing, the tagged Node collector on `f12d1c25` collected 7,563 test descriptors from the 756 files in the fork CI request. The two scheduler regression callbacks both passed. This was a focused check of the earlier revision.

## E2E user journeys

- The previously failing Idea Tree journey passed in an isolated local stack and in the [GitHub L2 E2E (mocked, standard-config) rerun](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45585984445/job/139112952177) for `c17479d718765c219bba22c3f279e320cfaeec85`. The journey verifies pause, manual resume, and three rounds of iteration. The [journey report and screenshots](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/45585984445/artifacts/15009777596) are available in the CI artifact.
- Chromium component checks verified the desktop provenance card and CSV row selection with fixed inputs. Full-stack journeys for CSV import, desktop paper display, run replay, and account check-in remain unverified.

## UI screenshots

Captured in Chromium using the repository's actual React components and styles with fixed evidence and CSV inputs. The desktop screenshots open the evidence card's provenance tab. The CSV screenshots open the Data table tab and click the same `sample#4` record with value `10`.

### Desktop evidence card

Before the review follow-up (`63b7bd13`), the paper card displays literal JATS tags. After the follow-up, the same input displays as two readable paragraphs, preserving `<LOD`, `>0`, and the text from the inline tags.

**Before**

![Desktop paper card before the follow-up](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8929ec3a-92af-4b10-9b3c-738e0b2aa8eb)

**After**

![Desktop paper card after the follow-up](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4111d6c6-027c-4d75-aa48-56343d47e904)

### Web CSV data table

Before the PR (`c3a2305a` parser), clicking one row highlights a second row with the same internal key. After the PR, only the clicked record is highlighted.

**Before**

![Web CSV table before the fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc7be5c1-aa5c-4c05-9b84-30164cca6a28)

**After**

![Web CSV table after the fix](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e3979dc9-eeaa-4f54-b293-e25a23105a31)

## Release

Release category: `release:fix`

User impact: CSV artifact rows retain distinct identities, paper text keeps literal comparisons, and saved research state and run history recover more reliably. The Idea Research card stays paused and keeps Continue available after a delayed refresh. Invalid check-in settings fail at startup with a configuration error.

Compatibility and migration: No data migration is required. Use non-negative decimal integers such as `0` or `100` for check-in settings. Unset an unused variable to use its default. Blank values, signed values, and scientific notation cause a startup configuration error.

1392.author: yuanzhou75
1392.body:
An Idea Tree stage gets exactly one correction when its answer is malformed. An empty or truncated answer did not: `research.py:351` raised before the branch that re-asks with `correction` and `previousResponse`, so `ask()` saw a failed activity and `run()` settled the whole research `interrupted` after a single call — a call that spent model tokens and could have been retried.

`transport()` returns the provider's `choices[0].message.content` verbatim (`research.py:279`), so an HTTP 200 whose content is empty or `null` is exactly what reaches this check. It is stage-agnostic: `design`, `ideate`, each assessor, `aggregate` and `propagate` all go through `_ask`.

## The change

The empty check now sits inside the same `try` as validation, so an empty answer takes the single correction: the model is told its previous answer was empty (`correction: empty or truncated model output; stage cannot continue`) and may answer again. A second empty answer still fails the stage, with `reason` naming the role, exactly as a malformed answer does.

```python
try:
    if raw is None or isinstance(raw, str) and not raw.strip():
        raise ValueError('empty or truncated model output; stage cannot continue')
    result = validate_result(role, parse_json(raw), {...})
```

## The policy behind it

This is the remaining half of #1327; the over-depth half was fixed in #1297 (trim to the ceiling, keep the removed direction as `trimmedDirection`), and a bad ideation round is already skipped at run level there. The issue asked which policy to take for an empty answer, and the release owner chose the first option on 2026-11-25: **route it through the existing single correction**. The two rejected alternatives, and why:

- **A separate retry budget for empty content** (2-3 resends with backoff): extra tokens and a second kind of retry to account for, for a failure that the existing correction already covers.
- **Degrade to `completed` when the answer stays unusable**: that turns a genuinely broken model into an apparent success. A second unusable answer still settles the research `interrupted` with the stage in `reason`, which is what keeps the failure visible.

## Tests

One test changes with the behaviour, deliberately and visibly, and two cases are added:

| Test | What it pins |
| --- | --- |
| `test_empty_or_truncated_stage_consumes_the_correction_and_preserves_usage` (was `…_preserves_usage_without_format_correction`) | `None`, `''` and `'  '` are each asked **twice**, the correction carries `empty or truncated`, both calls' tokens land (28), `reserved` returns to 0, the persisted activity is still `failed` and names the stage |
| `test_an_empty_answer_is_retried_once_and_can_succeed` | empty once, then a valid answer: `ask('design')` returns the result instead of raising, two calls, 28 tokens |
| `test_a_research_survives_an_empty_ideation_answer` | run level: the ideate stage answers empty once, the correction is enough, and the research settles `completed` with no budget or round loss |

## Cross-service artefacts this changes with it

The old contract was pinned outside `services/evolve` and both places move here:

- `services/api/src/protocol-compatibility.test.ts`, case `truncated-idea-stage` (tagged `category:st`, so it is the ST gate): it drives the real Python client through the real proxy, and now expects two upstream calls instead of one, 28 persisted tokens instead of 14, and the corrected failure message. `upstreamCalls` is per kind — 2 for this shape and for `transient-provider-error`, still 1 for `invalid-shape` and `truncated-hidden-reasoning` — and the case also asserts that both calls report their usage. The loop title no longer claims every deterministic shape is never retried.
- `docs/en/model-api-compatibility.md` and `docs/zh/model-api-compatibility.md`: the compatibility contract said an empty or truncated stage is stopped without a correction. Both now state the correction it actually gets and that a second empty answer still fails the stage, with the role in the reason.

## Validation

| Layer | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Engine UT | `pytest services/evolve/tests/test_idea_research.py` on a tree rebuilt from main `9c74af8b` | **44 passed** (42 on main + these two new cases) |
| Mutation | revert `research.py` to main and rerun the three cases | **3 failed** — the fix is what makes them pass |
| ST case, Python half | the `truncated-idea-stage` script run directly against a local 200 with `content: null`, `usage.total_tokens: 14` | 2 requests, 28 tokens, `reserved == 0`, activity `failed`, and the second request carries the new correction text — matches the updated assertions |
| `pnpm ci:st`, `tsc` | not run here | no `node_modules` on this host; the TypeScript half of the ST case is for CI |

Not claimed: no live L5 run (this file has no UI and no journey change).

Fixes #1327.
